exposure: AMA parity (primiparous, 2-5 births, 6-9 births, or ≥10 births)
cohort: 24,579 women with spontaneously-conceived singleton births, including 11,243 of advanced maternal age (≥35 years) and 13,336 aged 24-27 years
finding: Advanced maternal age, particularly among primiparous women, is associated with an increased incidence of adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes, including hypertension, diabetes, emergency cesarean sections, and large for gestational age infants, compared to younger women.
mod_finding: Emergency cesarean sections were significantly more frequent in advanced maternal age mothers, including primiparous women, compared to younger controls.
